summary:
## Core Concept: MCP Server for Cursor

This video guides you through building a custom **MCP (Model-Controller-Prompter)** server in Python and connecting it to the **Cursor IDE**. This allows AI agents within Cursor to use powerful, custom-built tools.

*   The entire server is implemented in a single Python file (`server.py`) with less than 35 lines of code.
*   It establishes a connection between Cursor's MCP client and your self-hosted server.

## Custom Tools Implemented

The server is equipped with two primary tools to enhance the agent's capabilities:

1.  **Linkup Web Search Tool**: Provides the agent with deep web research capabilities, allowing it to access and answer questions based on recent information not present in the LLM's training data. The search `depth` can be configured easily between `standard` and `deep`.

2.  **LlamaIndex RAG Tool**: Enables **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** over a local directory of documents. This allows the agent to securely query a private knowledge base (e.g., PDFs, project documents), creating a "Perplexity-like experience" inside the editor.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> By combining these tools, you give your Cursor agent access to both the live internet and your private, local data.

## Setup and Configuration in Cursor

To connect your custom server, follow these steps:

1.  In Cursor, navigate to **Settings > Cursor Settings**.
2.  Go to the **MCP** section and click **"Add a new MCP server"**.
3.  Provide a **Name** for your server (e.g., `Twitter demo`).
4.  Set the **Command** to start the server (e.g., `uv run python server.py`).
5.  Specify the **Directory** where your `server.py` file is located.

> [!TIP]
> The video recommends using `uv`, a fast Python package manager and runner, to execute the server startup command.

## Code and Architecture Highlights

*   **MCP Server**: The server is created using `FastMCP` from the `mcp-sdk` Python library.
*   **LlamaIndex Workflows**: The RAG tool is built using this feature, which organizes the process into a visual, graph-like structure with two main entry points:
    *   **Ingest Path**: This runs when the server starts, adding documents from your specified directory into the knowledge base.
    *   **Retrieve Path**: This is triggered by a user query. It finds relevant context from the knowledge base, uses an LLM to synthesize an answer, and returns the result to the user.
*   **Unified Interface**: MCPs provide a standardized interface for AI agents to interact with the external world, making it easy to integrate tools with hosts like Cursor, cloud platforms, or custom clients.
transcription:
## Introduction to the MCP Server Architecture

Hey everyone, welcome to this video and today I'm going to show you how to build your own MCP server and then connect it to your cursor ID. So before I jump into the demo, I quickly want to give you an overview of what we're building.

So the MCP host that we have is our cursor ID where we have an MCP client running. We're going to connect this client to the MCP server that we are going to build. So it's a single file implementation where it will do everything in just 30-35 lines of code. I'll show you in a bit like how it's done.

Then our server has two tools. One is a linkup web search tool that enables deep web research and we also have a llama index rag tool which is implemented using llama index workflows that enables you to do rag over any specified directory. So it's like having a perplexity like experience right from your cursor ID wherein you can do deep web research and you can also ground the generation of your agent based on a particular directory using the rack tool.

So without any further ado, let's jump into the demo.

## Setting Up the MCP Server in Cursor

Okay, so before I start the demo, if you're new here, make sure that you subscribe to my channel and also hit the like button so that it gives me a message that I should be creating more videos like this. Thank you so much.

So now I'm in my cursor ID and as you can see all the code is just under 35 lines of code and in this we have two tools. one is a web search tool that is implemented using linkup and then we also have a rack tool that is implemented using lamandex workflows. I'll also go over the details of each of these things like how they work but before that I would like you to show that how you can connect this to your cursor MCP client.

So all you need to do is to go to cursor go to settings and inside that we have cursor settings and there you would find an option for MCP. Next you just need to click on add a new MCP server. So you need to provide a name for your server which is, let's say, so I'm calling it as Twitter demo. And you also need to specify a command that how you can you know start this server. So it's a fairly simple command.

I'm using UV. If you're not already using UV I would recommend that you start doing so. It's a really great package manager. And then you specify the directory where exactly your server is located. So in this case I have given the complete path to my directory and then a run command. So it's just like a python run server.py command. So this would start our server and also connect it with the client. So let's click on add.

## Using the Web Search Tool

All right. So now it's connected and as we can see it already shows us that what tools are available. So we have a web search tool and we have a rag tool. So once you have this connected we can go to a new chat session and so in the chat session you need to make sure that you are using the agent mode because agents have ability to use all sort of tools whether they are custom built or whether they are MCP. So once you are in the agent mode you can start asking any questions.

So let's ask the first question. So my question is regarding a recent match that happened a couple of days ago between two teams in the Indian Premier League. So it's just a cricket league that is played every year in India. So this is something that would need web search otherwise it's not possible for any LLM to know like what has recently happened due to their knowledge cutoff. I'll also specify that use MCP tools and click send. Right?

As you can see it is saying that calling MCP tool and it also specifies the exact tool or the method name that we have in the server.py which is web search. So it'll run this tool. So we have some initial result and yeah so we also have a final coherent response wherein it says that Chennai Super Kings or CSK beat Mumbai Indians by four wickets in the IPL 2025 match. So it has all the details. So basically what I meant to show you is that we are able to successfully call the web tool through our cursor ID.

## Using the LlamaIndex RAG Tool

So now it's time to test out the second tool which is a rag tool and as you can see here that we have a rag tool and for the sake of this demo I am grounding all of the generation for this rag on this particular directory wherein I have a particular paper called deepseek.pdf but in your case like you can add any sort of a custom knowledge base or any document that is private to you that you want your cursor ID to have access to. So that can be added here. So let's get to the chat and ask it. So I'm asking it how is Deepseek R1 trained use MCP tools. Let's see how it works. 

Right. So it is automatically able to identify that it needs to use the rack tool and it is able to identify by looking at the command that I added over here. I mean you can specify this to be anything. So let's say your directory has documents related to employee on boarding or maybe like your financial documents. So you can specify all that thing in this description for this method and our agent would be automatically able to understand it.

So as you can see it successfully called the rack tool and we have a final answer on how deepc carb 1 was trained. So it gives a detailed explanation based on the paper that we provided like what are all the different stages and what exactly happened in them.

So yes the idea is to show you that now my cursor ID can have access to my custom knowledge base which can be anything that I provide in a certain directory and it can also do deep web research.

## Code Walkthrough: The Python MCP Server

Now that you have seen that how it actually works, it's time to do a code walk through. So again I'm in my server.py py script which implements my MCP server.

So in order to do this I'm using MCP's Python SDK right and so you can create this server using this fast MCP and you can specify the name of your server and after that we are going to use a linkup client. So this linkup client is something that lets us do deep web research and if you see the implementation in the tool so it just takes a query the depth. So basically if you want to do a standard search or you want to do deep web research. So all of this can be, you know, changed or toggled with just a single word. So instead of standard if I do deep then it would do deep web research just like you know what OpenAI is offering and what other webs tools are offering in this space.

And next is a rag tool.

## Understanding the LlamaIndex RAG Workflow

So in order to build this rag tool I have used llama index workflows. So I'll show you the code for the same as well. So this is all the code that we need to implement a rag workflow using lam index workflows. But to better understand this I would want to show you an image of how this workflow would look like. So you can easily, you know, once you create a workflow ll index offers a functionality wherein you can, you know, or you can plot all the different paths that a workflow can take and either you can save it as an HTML or a PNG so that you can easily visualize what exactly is happening in each of the steps.

So there's a start event that says that okay this is what triggers our workflow. So every time a start event can go to like multiple steps. So in this case our workflow has two entry points. One is an ingest entry point wherein you can use this to add new knowledge to our rag system and then there's a retrieve step wherein or this is another entry point wherein user can come up with a query and get answers to their query based on the knowledge base or based on the documents that have been already ingested.

So once we have this ingest event once the injection is finished we have a stop event that says that okay you need to stop the workflow here and we say that done okay this path is done you have already successfully ingested your knowledge base but in case like if user comes up with a new query so it will be using the retrieve step and it'll be using the second entry point of our workflow. So once you retrieve it will retrieve all the relevant nodes or the context from the knowledge that is already present and then we have a synthesis step. So in the synthesis step it is going to use the query as well as the retrieve documents which is used as a context and it will send it to the LLM and then LLM produces the final response and this is how the workflow works and I can quickly show you an example of this how you can run it.

So as you can see in this main method so we create an instance of the workflow we start the injection first right. So we would ingest all the documents that are present in the data directory and after that we are going to do a retrieval or we are going to fire up a query and get the response to it. So if I run it, yeah so we have the results here right. So this is how our workflow works.

## Final Implementation and Conclusion

And similarly we are calling it in the server that we have defined. So first whenever the server starts we make sure that the documents from the directory are ingested and ready for search and retrieval. So we call the ingest step of our workflow first right and then once we are inside the rag tool we get a user query that would be coming from our agent inside our cursor ID and this query would be received here and it would run the workflow against this query and fetch a relevant answer to it which is again going to be displayed here as you can see here. This is what we did last time.

So now the moral of the story is it's fairly simple to give your cursor ID access to any sort of tool in this world. Maybe it can be a vector database. Maybe it's a rack tool or maybe like it's an external API that you're calling or a tool like link up that can enable deep web research in just a few lines of code and your cursor ID can get access to it.

So MCPs are really powerful and what makes them really powerful is they provide a unified interface on how your agents can interact with the external world and it's fairly easy to integrate them with the ids like cursor cloud desktop and you can also build your custom client on the need basis. So I have shared all of this code in the next tweet and I hope you enjoyed this video and I'll see you in another one. Thanks for watching.
